body.statement: For the independent product experiment, the full and degree-restricted optima satisfy \(F_{\mathrm{prod}}=\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2F_j\) and \(F_{\mathrm{prod},r}=\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2F_{j,r}\), even when the comparison class contains joint observed-data interactions across blocks. Primal rules add and dual certificates tensor. For \(B\) identical copies of \(\mathfrak E_\star\) with \(a_j=1/B\), the optima are \(107/(72B)\) and \(55/(36B)\), and the gap is \(1/(24B)\).
body.proof_tex:
Write the schedule as \(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_B)\) on disjoint coordinate blocks and the assignment as \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_B)\).  By \(\text{ass:block-independence}\), for the aggregate score in \(\text{def:product-experiment}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 f_{\mathrm{prod}}(\theta)
 &=\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^Ba_jX_j(\theta_j)\right)\\
 &=\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2\operatorname{Var}\{X_j(\theta_j)\}
 =\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2f_j(\theta_j).
 \end{aligned}\tag{28}
\]
Fix local primal minimizers \(b_j\).  Each lifted \(b_j(\theta_j)\) is observable in the product experiment, and
\[
 b_{\mathrm{prod}}(\theta):=\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2b_j(\theta_j)
 \ge\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2f_j(\theta_j)=f_{\mathrm{prod}}(\theta). \tag{29}
\]
More explicitly, if \(g_{j,z_j}\) is an assignment-level table implementing \(b_j\), then the joint observed-data table
\[
 g_z^{\mathrm{prod}}:=\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2g_{j,z_j}
\]
implements \(b_{\mathrm{prod}}\); hence the primal construction uses no cross-block oracle information.
Under the product objective law, finite factorization gives
\[
 \mathbb E_qb_{\mathrm{prod}}=
 \sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2F_j,
\]
so (29) proves \(F_{\mathrm{prod}}\le\sum_ja_j^2F_j\).  If the local bounds have degree at most \(r\), the same sum has degree at most \(r\), giving
\(F_{\mathrm{prod},r}\le\sum_ja_j^2F_{j,r}\).

For the reverse inequalities, choose local dual optimizers \(\mu_j\) supplied by \(\text{thm:dual-complete-class}\), and put \(\mu=\bigotimes_{j=1}^B\mu_j\).  A product-observable monomial has a unique factorization
\[
 m_S(\theta)=\prod_{j=1}^Bm_{S_j}(\theta_j),
 \quad\quad S_j\subseteq O_{z_j}.
\]
Local margin equality and independence therefore imply
\[
 \mathbb E_\mu m_S
 =\prod_j\mathbb E_{\mu_j}m_{S_j}
 =\prod_j\mathbb E_{q_j}m_{S_j}
 =\mathbb E_qm_S. \tag{30}
\]
Thus \(\mu\) is feasible even against product observation sets that generate cross-block interactions.  Using (28),
\[
 \mathbb E_\mu f_{\mathrm{prod}}
 =\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2\mathbb E_{\mu_j}f_j
 =\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2F_j. \tag{31}
\]
Dual weak equality from \(\text{thm:dual-complete-class}\), together with the primal upper bound, proves the first formula.

For the restricted problem, the required local duality is a finite LP fact, not an extra assumption.  Let \(M_{j,r}\) have columns \(m_S\) for \(S\in\mathcal J_j\) with \(|S|\le r\).  The local restricted primal is \(\min\{(M_{j,r}^{\top}q_j)^{\top}\beta:M_{j,r}\beta\ge f_j\}\).  The constant bound makes it feasible, and full support of \(q_j\) makes every bounded sublevel set compact exactly as in \(\text{thm:dual-complete-class}\).  Applying that theorem's finite active-constraint cone argument with \(M\) replaced by \(M_{j,r}\) yields attainment and the matching restricted margin dual
\[
 F_{j,r}=\max_{\mu_j\ge0:\,M_{j,r}^{\top}\mu_j=M_{j,r}^{\top}q_j}
 \sum_{\theta_j}\mu_j(\theta_j)f_j(\theta_j).
\]
Choose an optimizer \(\mu_j\) from this displayed finite dual.  If a global observable monomial has total degree at most \(r\), then every \(|S_j|\le r\), so every factor in (30) is among the local restricted moment constraints.  Hence the same product is restricted-dual feasible, and the displayed dual equality gives
\[
 F_{\mathrm{prod},r}=\sum_{j=1}^Ba_j^2F_{j,r}.
\]
This also covers \(a_j=0\).  Finally, for identical copies of \(\mathfrak E_\star\) and \(a_j=1/B\), \(\text{thm:quartic-separation}\) gives
\[
 F_{\mathrm{prod}}=B\frac1{B^2}\frac{107}{72}=\frac{107}{72B},
 \quad\quad
 F_{\mathrm{prod},2}=F_{\mathrm{prod},3}
 =B\frac1{B^2}\frac{55}{36}=\frac{55}{36B},
\]
and subtraction gives the exact gap \(1/(24B)\).
body.justification: Tensorization shows that the finite separation survives normalization and unrestricted cross-block competitors at inferential scale.
body.gap: The matrix framework in \cite{Middleton2021Unifying} and the optimized quadratic theory in \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} provide no product law for all-degree observable spaces or exact higher-degree gaps.
body.consumer: Independently randomized small networks or blocks can reuse one certified lookup rule while retaining the exact advantage after aggregation.
